questions.question: Describe the key features that distinguish human language from animal communication systems.
questions.correctAnswer: Human language has: semanticity (meaning), generativity (infinite combinations), displacement (past/future), arbitrariness (no word-object connection), cultural transmission. Most animal communication lacks generativity and displacement - bees show some displacement but cannot create new messages.

questions.question: Evaluate whether apes can learn language, referring to studies of Washoe and Kanzi.
questions.correctAnswer: Washoe: learned 100+ ASL signs and combined them creatively. Suggests apes can learn aspects of language. However: Terrace argued Washoe's combinations were imitation, not syntax; the Gardners were accused of over-interpreting signs; apes don't develop language naturally. questions.question: Discuss whether the difference between human and animal communication is qualitative or quantitative.
questions.correctAnswer: Qualitative difference: humans have unique features (generativity, syntax) that animals lack entirely - a difference in kind. Quantitative difference: animals show some language abilities (semanticity, limited displacement, basic combinations) - a difference in degree.
